title: RDTRL — Can a network learn to write from reward alone?
description:
An experimental bench testing whether a neural network can learn to produce language from a scalar reward alone, with random initial weights, no pretraining and no input/output pairs. The search spaces are small enough to enumerate exhaustively, so validity mass, effective modes, the Gibbs optimum and the conditional structure are computed exactly rather than estimated.

Test 1 copies a fixed sentence and shows the success comes from reward decomposability rather than from search. Test 2 uses a hand-written grammar judged by a deterministic parser, reaching 99.9 percent grammaticality with no learned rule, and isolates the cause of mode collapse.

Version 0.3.0 adds a closed-form bound: a policy with no determiner-to-noun coupling has a product support, so at full validity it is capped by the largest fully valid product in the sublanguage it enters. That bound is never exceeded across 70 runs, is attained exactly by half of them, and turns out to be a plateau rather than a basin. Version 0.3.1 is a metadata release recording the acknowledgment below.

Version 0.4.0 adds the reversal test, which decides whether that bound is a law or a coincidence of vocabulary: a three-gender lexicon puts the two ceilings in a ratio of 3 instead of 2, which no relabelling can produce, and the observed maxima follow the prediction exactly. It also switches the advantage line to a single rounding, which turns out to be a better controlled experiment than a seed, since it perturbs the trajectory while leaving the initialisation bit-identical: 70 of 70 seeds keep their corner while only 21 of 70 keep their mode count.

Version 0.5.0 adds test 3, a referential game with 27 referents and 27 messages in which the optimum set, the null distribution and the gradient are all computed rather than estimated. All 27 factorial perfect codes earn exactly 1, so compositionality is 1296/27! of the optimum set before any training. The single-agent equal-optima certificate does not survive two agents: it requires the tied objects to be the support of the distribution whose entropy is in the objective, which codes are not. An equivariance argument replaces it and gives the same number for any equivariant algorithm, with the corollary that a free per-referent embedding table makes the whole procedure exchangeable on the referent side and therefore ties every code in advance, whatever is done on the message side. Measured over 100 seeds, any residual selection by the dynamics is smaller than 0.0087 in concentration. Channel noise breaks the symmetry while leaving the reward tie exact at every noise level, and produces nothing; population turnover preserves the symmetry and likewise produces nothing. Of everything tested, only the parametrization produced compositionality, and it did so by making the alternatives unrepresentable rather than by selecting among them. Sixteen refuted hypotheses are recorded with their dates, eight of them from this version alone, and none of them arithmetic errors.

Acknowledgment. The product bound is due to Dipankar Sarkar (ORCID 0000-0001-5431-6367), who derived the order-1 marginals independently from the published article and then showed that the two degenerate corners hold the same number of valid sentences but not the same largest product. Five rounds of his criticism also corrected a statistic that measured determiner coverage rather than agreement, a saturation metric that could exceed 100 percent, a sample-size claim that pooled three seeds into twenty-four rows, a falsification threshold derived from a sample maximum that estimates nothing, and a concentration statistic that let one attribute win two positions.
